title: Converting Types with From and Into
goal: Convert types safely using standard conversion traits.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Standard Traits

sections.text: You convert types explicitly in Rust using standard conversion traits. Rust avoids implicit type coercions to prevent subtle bugs.

sections.code:
let num = i32::from(42_i16);
let ip = std::net::Ipv4Addr::from([127, 0, 0, 1]);
sections.caption: From creates a target type from an input.

sections.text: The `From` trait defines how to construct a type from another input type. It represents a lossless and infallible conversion.

sections.code:
let num: i32 = 42_i16.into();
let ip: std::net::Ipv4Addr = [127, 0, 0, 1].into();
sections.caption: Into converts using the expected target type.

sections.text: Implementing `From<T> for U` automatically provides an implementation of `Into<U> for T`. You should implement `From` for your custom types.

explanation: Convert types safely using standard conversion traits.
